chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Hamzah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Do not eat the meat of the Jalalah, and if its sweat touches you, wash it off.

key_terms.الْجَلَّالَةِ: An animal that feeds primarily on impurities or unclean feed, making its meat makruh or haram depending on the school.
key_terms.عَرَقِهَا: Its sweat, referring to the bodily secretion of the Jalalah animal.
key_terms.لُحُومَ: Meat, specifically the flesh of animals.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating meat from animals that eat impurities (Jalalah) and their effect on ritual purity?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahar establishes the prohibition of consuming meat from the 'Jalalah'—animals whose diet consists predominantly of impurities—and extends the ruling to ritual purity by requiring the washing of sweat that contacts the body. In Shia jurisprudence, this highlights the principle that an animal's internal state, derived from its feed, affects both its culinary permissibility and its physical impurity (najāsah). The instruction to wash the sweat underscores the practical application of removing subtle impurities to maintain ritual cleanliness for prayer.
